Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: t021600-dot
Message:
The database is live: schema applied, verified, and se-m6 audit run for real

Applied six migrations to the live project kqboenytmzagdiweqygl - tables and
RLS, helpers and column grants, the policies, views and write paths, the agent
paths and validation, and the advisor fix.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE DATABASE. Every check returns rows only on failure;
one row came back and it is the expected one:
  RLS off anywhere ..................... none (8/8 tables on)
  view without security_invoker ........ none (3/3 on)
  anon holds any table grant ........... none
  service_role holds any table grant ... none
  password-ish column anywhere ......... none            <- se-m3 PROVEN
  definer fn without pinned search_path  none
  RLS on with no policy ................ app_settings, correct - the kill switch

se-m6 IS NOW REAL, not a template. Supabase's own Security Advisor found two
trigger functions - missions_guard() and rls_auto_enable() - exposed as
PostgREST endpoints callable by anon without signing in. missions_guard is the
one carrying the rate limit, the kill switch and the line that forces
researcher_id to the caller. Revoked execute on both, re-ran the linter, both
findings gone. The six that remain are authenticated-only and deliberate.
Before and after in 03-security/evidence/.

config.js now holds the live project URL and publishable key. gitleaks
allowlists that one finding with the reason written in - and the pre-commit
hook still blocks a real JWT in that exact file, tested just now by pasting a
fake service-role key and watching the commit refuse.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: t021600-dot
Message:
Unblock the whole build: vendor supabase-js, load it, and close the 404

Three things that each stopped the product working at all.

1. The root landing page's only button pointed at signin.html, which does not
   exist anywhere in the repo. The first click a judge makes on the deployed
   site was a 404, which is fe-m1 and fe-m2 gone in one click. The real file
   is login.html.

2. supabase-js was in no file anywhere, and our CSP forbids a CDN. Vendored at
   a pinned 2.45.4 into app/vendor/supabase.js.

3. js/config.js was loaded by ZERO of the six pages, so window.sb never
   existed and the se-m1 proof script could not run at all. Every page now
   loads vendor/supabase.js then js/config.js, before data.js uses them.

config.js also no longer calls createClient() at the top level. It used to
throw when supabase-js was missing - and because that throw happens inside
its own script tag, the four later scripts still loaded and the app carried
on against mock data looking completely fine. A demo that passes on stage
while touching no database is the worst failure shape available. It now warns
loudly and leaves sb null.

.gitleaksignore added for ONE verified false positive in the minified vendor
bundle, with the fingerprint and the reason - never a blanket vendor ignore.
